<description>
A program that answers on the Tor control port can hang the node at shutdown and point its onion connections at another host.

I now accept the cookie file named in the PROTOCOLINFO reply only if it is a regular file. A FIFO made `fopen()` block the torcontrol thread, and shutdown waits for that thread. On POSIX the file is opened with `O_NONBLOCK`, so a swap to a FIFO after the check does not block either.

I also use the SOCKS listener from `GETINFO net/listeners/socks` only if it is on the control port's host. That is a loopback address if the control port is on loopback, and the `-torcontrol` host otherwise. Other listeners, including unix sockets, are ignored and a warning is logged. The program can no longer name another host.

If no listener qualifies, I keep the onion proxy set by `-proxy` instead of replacing it with `127.0.0.1:9050`. A remote Tor whose SOCKS listener is on the `-torcontrol` host keeps working. A remote Tor that listens for SOCKS on another address now needs `-onion`, or a `-proxy` that points to it.

Two cases stay open. A program on a loopback control port can still name a loopback listener of its own, and a regular file on a filesystem whose read never returns can still block shutdown.

Tests:
- a unit test for the listener rule in `torcontrol_tests`;
- a FIFO case in `util_tests`;
- functional tests in `feature_torcontrol.py`, with the mock Tor server, for the cookie file and the listeners.

`doc/tor.md` says that the control port is trusted, and a release note describes the change.
</description>

<commits>
6d994c29f1 torcontrol: Only read a regular file as authentication cookie

The path of the cookie file comes from the reply to PROTOCOLINFO, so
whatever answers on the control port chooses it. A FIFO with no writer
made fopen() block the torcontrol thread for good, and shutdown waits
for that thread.

Check that the path is a regular file before reading it, and log a
warning if it is not or cannot be examined. Also have ReadBinaryFile
open the file with O_NONBLOCK on POSIX systems, so that a file replaced
by a FIFO after the check cannot block either.

e445a64d7e torcontrol: Only use a SOCKS listener on the Tor control host

The reply to GETINFO net/listeners/socks is used as the proxy for onion
addresses. Whoever answers on the control port can name any address,
and all onion connections then go through it.

Only accept a listener on the host that runs the control port: a
loopback address if the control port is on loopback, otherwise the
address the control port was reached at. Log a warning for each other
listener, including a unix socket. This keeps working a remote Tor
reached with -torcontrol, which a loopback-only rule would break.

If no listener is accepted, keep the onion proxy that is already set,
such as the one from -proxy, instead of replacing it with 127.0.0.1:9050.
Without one, the default 127.0.0.1:9050 is still used. A listener on
127.0.0.1 is still preferred over other accepted ones.

3e9e292a1d doc: Say that the Tor control port is trusted

Bitcoin Core connects to 127.0.0.1:9051 by default whenever it listens,
even if Tor is not running. Document that whatever answers there is
trusted, for instance for the onion address the node advertises.
</commits>
